# Norway AADT Sensor Placement — Pipeline Overview

This document describes the full two-stage pipeline for selecting new traffic sensor locations
that maximally reduce prediction uncertainty on unmeasured road links.

## Goal

Given a road network where only a subset of links have measured AADT (Annual Average Daily Traffic),
select k new sensor locations such that placing sensors there reduces posterior uncertainty as much
as possible across all unmeasured links.

---

## Stage 1 — Spatial Prediction with INLA

The first stage fits a Besag-proper RBF spatial model via INLA to produce posterior predictions
on all links, including unmeasured ones.

### Data preparation

Traffic links are loaded from `data/prepared_traffic_links_norway.rds`. Each row is a directed
link (suffixed `-WITH` or `-AGAINST`). Key columns:

| Column | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `aadt` | Measured count; `NA` for unmeasured links |
| `functionalRoadClass` | Road class (0 = motorway, 7 = local) |
| `roadCategory` | Administrative category |
| `lastYearAadt_logAadt` | Log of prior-year AADT (continuous covariate) |
| `spatial.idx` | Integer index 1:n for the spatial effect |

### Model fitting

```r
model <- fit_inla_rbf_model(
  data               = prepared_traffic_links,
  adjacency_matrix   = adjacency_matrix,
  spatial_term       = "besagproper_rbf",
  similarity_covariates = selected_covariates,
  fixed_effects      = covariates,
  iid_effects        = "roadSystem",
  family             = "nbinomial"
)
```

The RBF (radial basis function) kernel weights the spatial precision matrix by link similarity.
Hyperparameters `tau`, `d`, `sigma` are estimated from data. Posterior means are stored in
`inla_pred` on the data frame.

See `docs/functions/inla-modeling.Rmd` for full function reference.

---

## Stage 2 — Greedy Mutual Information Sensor Selection

The second stage uses the posterior covariance structure from Stage 1 to greedily select
sensor locations maximizing mutual information (MI) gain (Krause et al. 2008).

### Flow conservation pre-processing

Before selection, links that can be derived from flow conservation equations are identified
and excluded from the candidate set:

```r
data_with_derivable <- identify_derivable_nodes(
  data             = prepared_traffic_links,
  nodes            = traffic_nodes,
  adjacency_matrix = adjacency_matrix
)
```

See `docs/functions/flow-conservation.Rmd`.

### Covariance matrix construction

```r
cov_result <- create_covariance_and_precision_matrix(
  adjacency_matrix = adjacency_matrix,
  tau = model$tau, d = model$d, sigma = model$sigma,
  distances        = model$distances,
  data             = prepared_traffic_links,
  with_and_against = TRUE
)
```

The `with_and_against = TRUE` flag applies the C·Σ·Cᵀ transformation to aggregate
directional link uncertainties to road-level (since sensors measure both directions).

### Greedy selection

```r
result <- greedy_mi_sensor_selection_norway(
  data              = data_with_derivable,
  covariance_matrix = cov_result$covariance_matrix_sum,
  ids               = cov_result$ids,
  k_per_county      = 100,
  r                 = 100,
  weighting_bias    = c(1, 1, 0.9, 0.7, 0.5, 0.3, 0.1, 0),
  frc_aadt_alpha    = 0.9,
  neighbourhood_decay = c(1, 0.5, 0.1)
)
```

See `docs/functions/sensor-selection.Rmd` for full parameter reference.

---

## Output

Results are saved as `.rds` files in `results/production/`:

```r
saveRDS(result, "results/production/frc_sqrt(0.9_to_0)_100percounty_100overall.rds")
```

Each file contains:

```r
list(
  selected_data_entries = <sf data frame>,   # selected links with mi_score
  summary = list(
    n_selected   = integer,
    k_per_county = integer,
    r            = integer,
    counts_table = data.frame               # per-county breakdown
  )
)
```

Results are visualised in the Shiny app (`shiny/app.R`). See the deploy rule in
`.github/instructions/shiny.instructions.md` before adding new results.

---

## Main Pipeline Script

`serious-testing/testing-sensor-selection-norway.R` is the entry point. Run it top-to-bottom
to reproduce all results. It sources `serious-testing/scripts_inla_sensor_placement.R` which
contains all 19 core functions.
